title: COSM: A Cooperative Scheduling Framework for Concurrent PIM and CPU Execution on Mobile Devices
evidence_span: COSM addresses concurrent processing-in-memory and CPU execution on mobile devices, where bank conflicts and shared-bus congestion can erase PIM benefits. It introduces a low-interference PIM control interface, an idleness-aware scheduler that inserts PIM commands into CPU idle windows, and overlap of PIM execution with data transfer. The abstract reports up to 2.8x PIM throughput and less than 2.0% CPU performance loss across concurrent LLM, mobile-app, and compute-kernel workloads.
problem: Mobile on-device LLM and application workloads can benefit from processing in memory, but CPU/PIM concurrency in shared memory is vulnerable to bank conflicts, bus congestion, and interference with CPU accesses.
method_or_artifact: A low-interference PIM control interface and idleness-aware cooperative scheduler that places PIM commands into idle windows in the CPU access sequence, hiding PIM latency while overlapping PIM work with data transfer.
workload_or_benchmark: Concurrent LLM workloads, mobile applications, and compute kernels evaluated with CPU and PIM execution on a shared-memory mobile-device setting.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Mobile CPU/PIM systems sharing DRAM banks and buses; exact memory technology, PIM substrate, platform configuration, and energy model require full-paper verification.
baselines: CPU-only execution for the evaluated concurrent workloads
metrics: concurrent LLM, mobile-app, and compute-kernel evaluation
limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; exact platform details, PIM command costs, scheduler overhead, energy impact, workload mix, and comparisons against all relevant PIM schedulers require full-paper verification.

title: Cerberus: Cross-Layer ECC Co-Design for Robust and Efficient Memory Protection
evidence_span: Cerberus co-designs on-die ECC, link ECC, and system ECC for dense, high-speed DRAM. Its Encode-Once, Decode-Many design reuses controller encoding for link-level write detection/retry, device repair on reads, and system-level end-to-end recovery. The paper combines complementary parity/syndrome structures, decoder ordering, and a correction budget intended to avoid miscorrection amplification and reports improved resilience to clustered and peripheral faults with reduced redundant overhead in an HBM context.
problem: Independent evolution of on-die, link, and system ECC creates duplicated redundancy, gaps, and cross-layer interference as DRAM density and I/O speed increase.
method_or_artifact: A cross-layer ECC architecture using Encode-Once, Decode-Many, complementary parity and syndrome structures, ordered decoding, and a correction budget that coordinates recovery across the memory stack.
workload_or_benchmark: Fault-injection and memory-protection evaluation for clustered and peripheral memory faults, with an HBM-oriented context; exact fault distributions and workloads require full-paper verification.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Dense high-speed DRAM and HBM-style memory stacks with on-die, link, and system ECC layers; results depend on the assumed fault model, interface organization, and controller/device cooperation.
baselines: independently layered on-die, link, and system ECC
limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; exact codeword layouts, fault-model probabilities, decoder latency, area/energy overhead, HBM generation, and quantitative baseline tables must be extracted from the full paper before making deployment or superiority claims.
